# Threads {#sec-threads}

biyos keeps no global state. Everything a call reads or changes belongs to an environment or to a model made on it, so environments are independent of each other and separate threads may use separate environments at the same time. Threads may also share one environment:

- Calls on different models of the environment may run at the same time, from any threads, and so may calls that only read the same model.
- A call that changes or frees a model runs alone on it: no other thread is in a call on that model meanwhile.
- A call that changes the environment itself, setting an option, adding or removing a hook or freeing it, overlaps no other call on the environment or on its models. Creating a model on it is not such a change.
- `BIYOS_interrupt` may overlap any call ([Interrupting a call](#sec-threads-interrupt)).

A program that wants to change one model from several threads gives each thread a copy (@sec-copy), on the same environment or on another. `BIYOS_copymdl` only reads the source, so other threads may read it meanwhile. Afterwards the two are apart.

An environment keeps a last error per thread ([The last error](#sec-errors-message)), so a thread reads the failure of its own last failed call, never one another thread left, together with the model that call was on.

biyos starts no thread of its own yet. `BIYOS_version` reads no state and may be called from any thread. A hook runs on the thread whose call sent the event, so the calls that read or format an event run there too. The hooks of an environment run one at a time: an event sent from one thread waits while a hook runs for another, so a hook needs no lock of its own, and `BIYOS_getevtmdl` tells which model each event came from. A hook must not wait for a call on another thread that sends an event on the same environment, since that event waits for the hook.

## Interrupting a call {#sec-threads-interrupt}

`BIYOS_interrupt` asks the call running on an environment to stop. Any thread may call it while another thread is inside a call on that environment or on one of its models, and so may a signal handler, since it only sets a flag and returns. A long call reads the flag where it checks its time limits and stops with the termination `BIYOS_TRM_STOP`, an outcome rather than an error code. The flag clears when the next call on the environment or on one of its models starts, so a request that arrives after a call has returned does not stop the one that follows. A call made by a hook leaves it set, so a hook may stop the call that sent its event. No call is long enough to read the flag yet.

## In Python {#sec-threads-python}

The package calls the library through `ctypes`, which releases the global interpreter lock for the length of each C call, so threads that work on separate environments run their C code side by side. In Python, one environment and its models are used by one thread at a time.

```{.python file="examples/python/threads.py"}
```

Each thread builds its own model on its own environment, and the results come back in the order the work was given, whatever order the threads finished in. A hook written in Python takes the interpreter lock while it runs.

`Env.interrupt` makes the request that [Interrupting a call](#sec-threads-interrupt) describes, and another thread may call it while a call runs. A `KeyboardInterrupt` raised in a hook makes it too, and is raised once the call returns.
